extracted.intended_audience: researchers, systematic reviewers and meta-researchers studying publication bias and outcome reporting (also journal editors/statisticians)
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction and evaluation of cohort studies measuring publication or outcome-reporting bias (manuscripts/abstracts/trials/regulatory submissions): classifying outcomes, measuring publication/acceptance rates, and estimating associations using regression. Focus is on methods and metrics used to detect selective publication or selective outcome reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome classification (statistical significance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcome classification: 1. Statistically significant (p < 0.05) for the primary outcome 2. Statistically non-significant 3. Unclear
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by multiple manuscript-cohort studies (e.g. Olson et al., Lee et al.) to categorise studies by the statistical significance of their primary outcome; forms the basis for comparing publication/acceptance rates between 'significant' and 'non-significant' studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome classification (positive/negative/not analysable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcome classification: 1. Positive or favourable or significant 2. Negative or non-supportive or no difference 3. Not analysable – unclear
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative wording used in some cohorts where authors labelled results as 'positive/favourable' vs 'negative/non-supportive' vs 'unclear' for analyses of publication likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome classification (positive/negative/neutral/not applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcome classification: 1. Positive – favoured experimental item 2. Negative – favoured existing standard of care over the experimental item 3. Neutral – no difference 4. Not applicable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in clinical/intervention manuscript cohorts (e.g. Okike et al.) to capture direction of effect rather than only statistical significance; informs subgrouping for acceptance/publication comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion of studies with different results
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of studies with different results: e.g., 51.4% (n = 383) with significant results; 45.7% (n = 341) with non-significant results; 2.8% (n = 21) with unclear results
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the distribution (percent and n) of cohort items across the outcome-classification categories; commonly presented in tables as the primary descriptive metric of the cohort's result profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance rate / publication rate by outcome category
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance rate: e.g., 20.4% (78/383) for significant results; 15.0% (51/341) for non-significant results; 19.0% (4/21) for unclear results
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate and report the proportion (numerator/denominator and %) of items in each outcome category that were accepted or published; used to quantify differential publication likelihood by result direction/significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical comparison using logistic regression / odds ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: Logistic regression analysis: significant vs non-significant results OR = 1.30 (95% CI: 0.87 to 1.96)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use regression models (logistic) to estimate the association between outcome category (e.g., significant vs non-significant) and publication/acceptance, reporting effect measures (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals; can be unadjusted or adjusted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multivariate (adjusted) analysis comparing outcome groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Multivariate analysis: positive vs nonpositive OR = 0.92 (95% CI: 0.62 to 1.35)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust for potential confounders in multivariable models when assessing the effect of outcome direction on publication/acceptance; report adjusted ORs and CIs and describe covariates included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting completeness of outcomes (fully/partially/not reported)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify each pre-specified outcome as fully reported, partially reported or not reported
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in outcome-reporting-bias studies to quantify completeness of outcome reporting; report proportions of outcomes in each completeness category and examples of partial reporting (e.g., missing effect size, missing p-value).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome reporting bias definition (selective reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcome reporting bias defined as discrepancies between outcomes specified in protocols/registrations and those reported in publications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect by comparing trial protocols/registries or other pre-specified documents with the published report; classify discrepancies (omitted outcomes, introduced outcomes, changed primary/secondary outcomes) and quantify frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit of analysis (manuscripts / abstracts / trials / scientific articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unit of analysis: manuscripts, abstracts presented at conferences, trials submitted to regulatory authorities, or manuscripts submitted to journals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify and use the appropriate unit (manuscript, abstract, trial) consistently when measuring publication bias; affects denominators for acceptance/publication rates and follow-up procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up duration to ascertain publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow-up (years) to determine publication status (reported as e.g. years to ascertain whether items were published or accepted)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report length of follow-up (time between submission/abstract/conference and search for publication) because shorter follow-up may underestimate publication rates; commonly reported in cohort characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohort inclusion/exclusion criteria (types of submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: 'Cohort study of 1107 manuscripts of original research (including qualitative research, excluding single case reports) submitted to BMJ, Lancet and Annals of Internal Medicine during 01–03/2003 and during 11/2003–02/2004'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define exactly which submissions/studies were eligible (journals, time windows, study types included or excluded) because cohort composition influences generalisability and observed publication bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of publication outcome (accepted/published vs not)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification of outcome: items classified as accepted/published versus not accepted/published (used as the primary outcome variable in publication-bias cohorts)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether 'accepted' refers to acceptance at initial submission, eventual publication in any journal, or publication in the original target journal; use consistent definitions and report numerators/denominators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison of publication rates by direction/significance with p-values
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical testing of differences in publication/acceptance rates (e.g., 'Difference in publication rate between positive and negative outcomes was not statistically significant (p = 0.41)')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform and report hypothesis tests (chi-square, Fisher's exact, or regression-based p-values) for differences in rates across outcome groups; accompany with effect estimates and CIs where possible.
